---
title: "Generate a Cross-Dialect SQL Date Series"
pagetitle: "Generate a Cross-Dialect SQL Date Series — seq_date_sql"
---

::: {.qrtdown-source .dont-index}
Source: [`R/utils-misc.R`](https://codeberg.org/usrbinr/ti/src/branch/main/R/utils-misc.R)
:::

<p>Creates a lazy <code>dbplyr</code> table containing a continuous sequence of dates.
The function automatically detects the SQL dialect of the connection and
dispatches the most efficient native series generator (e.g., <code>GENERATE_SERIES</code>
for DuckDB/Postgres or <code>GENERATOR</code> for Snowflake).
</p>

## Usage

```r
seq_date_sql(
  .con,
  start_date,
  end_date,
  calendar_type = "standard",
  time_unit = "day",
  week_start = 7,
  fiscal_year_start = 1
)
```

## Arguments

<dl class="qrtdown-arguments">
<dt id="arg-con"><code>.con</code><a class="anchor" aria-label="anchor" href="#arg-con"></a></dt>
<dd><p>A valid DBI connection object (e.g., DuckDB, Postgres, Snowflake)
or a <code>dbplyr</code> simulated connection.</p></dd>
<dt id="arg-start-date"><code>start_date</code><a class="anchor" aria-label="anchor" href="#arg-start-date"></a></dt>
<dd><p>A character string in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format or a Date object
representing the start of the series.</p></dd>
<dt id="arg-end-date"><code>end_date</code><a class="anchor" aria-label="anchor" href="#arg-end-date"></a></dt>
<dd><p>A character string in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format or a Date object
representing the end of the series.</p></dd>
<dt id="arg-time-unit"><code>time_unit</code><a class="anchor" aria-label="anchor" href="#arg-time-unit"></a></dt>
<dd><p>A character string specifying the interval. Must be one of:
<code>"day"</code>, <code>"week"</code>, <code>"month"</code>, <code>"quarter"</code>, or <code>"year"</code>.</p></dd>
<dt id="arg-week-start"><code>week_start</code><a class="anchor" aria-label="anchor" href="#arg-week-start"></a></dt>
<dd><p>description</p></dd>
</dl>

## Value

<p>A <code>tbl_lazy</code> (SQL) object with a single column <code>date</code>.
</p>

## Details

<p>This function is designed to be "nestable," meaning the resulting SQL can be
used safely inside larger <code>dplyr</code> pipelines. It avoids <code>WITH</code> clauses in
dialects like DuckDB to prevent parser errors when <code>dbplyr</code> wraps the query
in a subquery (e.g., <code style="white-space: pre;">⁠SELECT * FROM (...) AS q01⁠</code>).
</p>
<p>For unit testing, the function supports <code>dbplyr</code> simulation objects. If a
<code>TestConnection</code> is detected, it returns a <code>lazy_frame</code> to avoid metadata
field queries that would otherwise fail on a mock connection.
</p>
